hero.h1: Plumbing Maintenance in Highland Park, IL
hero.sub: Most plumbing problems start small: a few roots in the sewer line, a water heater past its prime, a valve that won't close. A whole-home plumbing inspection catches them early. Serving Highland Park and the North Shore.

img.alt: Plumber checking the drain and supply lines under a bathroom vanity during routine maintenance

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.intro: A maintenance visit looks at the whole system, not just the fixture that's bothering you:

steps.body: Age, leaks, the relief valve and sediment. A flush if it's due. See [water heater repair](/highland-park/water-heater-repair).
Slow drains, gurgling and signs of trouble in the main line. A [camera inspection](/highland-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) if something looks off.
Faucets, toilets, shutoff valves and supply lines for drips, leaks and parts that are wearing out.
A test cycle, the float, the check valve and battery backup. See [sump pumps](/highland-park/sump-pumps).
Corrosion, leaks and pipes at risk of freezing in basements, crawl spaces and garages.
What looks good, what to keep an eye on and what needs attention now, in plain English.

blocks.h2: Why Maintenance Matters in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: About 45% of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and about 1 in 4 before 1940. Homes from those years often have clay sewer pipe, cast iron drains or galvanized water lines, and all of them wear out with age.

items.body: An older system can run for years with the right care. An inspection tells you where it stands, so you can plan repairs instead of reacting to a leak.
In Highland Park, the homeowner owns the private sewer line from the house to the city main. The city's flood tips recommend having it checked for roots and debris.
Long Lake County winters are hard on outdoor spigots, pipes in exterior walls and water heaters. A fall check is the best time to catch problems.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: A maintenance visit stays a maintenance visit, not a sales pitch for something bigger.

steps.body: We check the whole system and show you what we find.
We'll tell you straight if everything looks good. If something needs attention, we'll tell you what and why, and how soon.
If you want anything fixed, you get a flat-rate price before any work begins.

blocks.h2: Plumbing Maintenance Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: How often should I have my plumbing inspected?
items.preview: Once a year for older homes, ideally in the fall.
items.answer: Once a year is a good rule for older homes, ideally in the fall before winter. Newer homes with modern materials can often go longer between checks.

items.q: My home was built before 1960. Is it at higher risk?
items.preview: It can be. An inspection tells you where your older system stands.
items.answer: It can be. Homes from those years often have clay sewer pipe, cast iron drains or galvanized water lines, and all of them wear out with age. Age alone doesn't mean something is wrong. An inspection tells you where your system stands.

items.preview: Yes, the No Drip Club. See the details below.
items.answer: Yes. The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club/) is our annual plan that brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance. See the details below.

items.q: How much does a plumbing inspection cost?
items.preview: It depends on the home and what's included. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the size of the home and what's included, like a sewer camera inspection or a water heater flush. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
